rubrics.criterion: The minimum-bump classifier no longer contains an inlined re-implementation of the token-list diffing algorithm; it derives the bump by calling the library's single shared list-diff routine (or an equivalent shared computation that centrally reports added, removed, and changed tokens) and classifies from those results.
rubrics.rationale: The classifier hosting a full copy of the diff algorithm is the deepest flattening in this instance; removing exactly that copy (by delegation, not by re-authoring the diff) is the core resolution for this task.

rubrics.criterion: The version-update predicate decides strict 'update is newer than base' semantics by delegating the ordering decision to the library's shared version-ordering helper (or an equivalent single shared ordering function), replacing its hand-rolled early-return ladder over major/minor/patch.
rubrics.rationale: The predicate's guard ladder is an inlined copy of the shared comparator's responsibility; only restoring the delegation edge resolves it. A repaired predicate that still hand-rolls the component comparison keeps the smell.

rubrics.criterion: The diff routine's per-field change detection calls a well-scoped, reusable, module-scope helper that owns the shallow per-property value-comparison rule (strict equality, then type mismatch, then element-wise array comparison), instead of embedding those comparison branches directly in its scan loop; the helper is a directly callable module-scope function, not a closure nested inside one consumer.
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately deleted the module-scope comparison helper and embedded its logic at the call site, so the responsibility lost its only named implementation. Any repair that leaves the comparison branches inside the loop (or hides them in a consumer-local closure) does not restore the reusable method the smell requires.

rubrics.criterion: All flattening instances in the versioning/comparison subsystem are repaired in the same patch set: beyond the largest monolith, the two subtler sites — the comparison logic embedded in the diff's change-detection loop and the hand-rolled ordering ladder in the update predicate — are also undone, so after the patch no entry point in this subsystem still re-implements a shared algorithm inside itself.
rubrics.rationale: The task's instruction states the pattern appears in more than two places and that missing any leaves the divergence problem in place; the two smaller copies use different idioms and different file locations, so a repair covering only the most visible site must not pass.

rubrics.criterion: The package's public API remains source-compatible after the refactor: every exported function, type, and enum keeps its exact name and signature — including the shared ordering helper and the list-diff routine that inlined callers used to bypass — and the package entrypoint still re-exports the same surface.
rubrics.rationale: The shared helpers survive as public API with external consumers, so a repair that deletes, renames, or re-signatures them to 'force' delegation breaks the recorded compatibility constraint of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The restored layout keeps helpers independent of their consumers: shared logic lives at module scope in the module that owns it (or is imported from a dedicated helper location), no helper begins importing one of its consumers or the classifier, and no circular imports are introduced among the versioning modules.
rubrics.rationale: The task instruction records this dependency-direction constraint explicitly; a repair that 'shares' logic by moving it into a consumer, or that wires modules cyclically, would trade one structural problem for another.

rubrics.criterion: The versioning primitives that were bypassed remain the shared implementations the entry points now use: the ordering comparator, the enum-owning upgrade classifier, and the next-version computation keep their behavior and are not themselves re-implemented, repurposed, or functionally rewritten by the repair (apart from import/wiring needed by their callers).
rubrics.rationale: These modules were innocent bystanders of the flattening; a patch that also churns them increases review burden without moving the smell, so their preservation is an instance-specific expectation.

rubrics.criterion: All scaffolding that existed only to support the inlined copies is removed with them: the composite 'chainId:address' Map index and update-membership Set with their boolean bookkeeping flags, the unrolled comparison branches and guard-ladder branches, and any imports or type-only imports that became needed only because of the copies — leaving no dead code, unused imports, or stale explanatory comments about the former flattened data flow.
rubrics.rationale: These artifacts were introduced by the intrusion solely to let the monolithic bodies work; leaving them behind (or leaving the comments describing them) marks an incomplete consolidation and misleads future maintainers.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, each shared responsibility — version ordering, list diffing, and per-field shallow value comparison — has exactly one implementation in the codebase; no second re-implemented copy of any of them survives anywhere (for example inside the classifier or the predicate).
rubrics.rationale: The maintenance problem this instance models is rule duplication across structurally divergent copies; the repair must end in a one-implementation-per-responsibility state, which is what future maintainers actually observe.

rubrics.criterion: The update predicate's strict-greater semantics are broken in the patched code — for example a version equal to (or older than) the base starts returning true, an operand order is flipped so some older versions read as updates, or equal components are treated as a difference.
rubrics.rationale: Rewriting the delegated ordering as an unrolled ladder is exactly the situation in which strictness and operand order are silently changed; this is the most plausible case-specific regression when restoring the predicate.

rubrics.criterion: The consolidated value comparison changes observable semantics relative to the task's starting state — for example it introduces deep/structural equality for nested object-valued fields (so equal-valued nested objects stop being reported as changed), flips the array comparison so the base array acts as the matching prefix instead of the updated array, requires equal lengths, or starts ignoring fields explicitly set to undefined.
rubrics.rationale: The task instruction pins the library's intentionally quirky comparison limitations; merging three divergent-looking copies into one helper is precisely where an author 'fixes' the quirks without being asked, silently changing which fields count as changed.

rubrics.criterion: The bump classification precedence is altered in the patched code, so a list change containing a removal can yield a non-MAJOR result (for example additions or field changes outrank removals and a removal plus additions returns MINOR or PATCH), or added tokens start counting as changes on their own.
rubrics.rationale: The classifier's precedence ladder (removal over addition over change) is a documented observable contract of this instance; re-deriving classification after extraction is the likely moment for the ordering to be silently rewritten.

rubrics.criterion: The diff output contract regresses in the patched code: added tokens no longer appear in first-encounter order of the update list, removed tokens no longer appear in base-list order, changed entries are no longer keyed by chain and then address, or a changed token's field-name list no longer follows the updated token's own key order (including fields set to undefined).
rubrics.rationale: These ordering and keying details are observable to every consumer of the diff and were deliberately preserved by the intrusion; repairs that re-scan lists on their own (instead of preserving the algorithm) commonly reorder or rekey the result.
